event_check: I read the full ASX per-issuer archive for 2023 to 2026 (https://www.asx.com.au/asx/v2/statistics/announcements.do?by=asxCode&asxCode=IPX&timeframe=Y&year=2026). The newest 2026 row is 24/09/2026 08:21 'Becoming a substantial holder'. There is no Annual Report yet, no 'Notice of Results' or results-date notice, and no webinar notice. Past annual-report dates are 18/09/2023 (evening), 27/09/2024 09:03 and 30/09/2025 09:44, so the lodgement drifts toward the 30 September statutory deadline. In 2026 the 30th is a Wednesday, which leaves 28, 29 and 30 September all open. The external calendars disagree with each other. TradingView says 28 September. MarketBeat projected 23 September (https://www.thecerbatgem.com/2026/09/21/iperionx-ipx-projected-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-wednesday.html) and that date passed with nothing lodged. The same page lists a call on 'Tuesday Sep 29 2026 7:00 PM ET', which is 30 September 09:00 AEST: outside the window, and it looks like last year's 29 Sep 19:44 ET release carried forward rather than a notice. ad-hoc-news cited '23 and 24 September' (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/unternehmensnachrichten/iperionx-lands-second-army-order-as-share-price-tests-fresh-lows-ahead-of/70100089), which also passed with nothing. EDGAR (CIK 1898601) shows IPX still files as a foreign private issuer on 6-K, with the 20-F usually in October (2025-10-15), so the audited accounts will not reach the market any earlier through the SEC. My estimate that the release lands inside the 2026-09-28 window is about one in three. It is unconfirmed, so I sized nothing.
session_check: If it lands, it is almost certainly bmo: every one of IPX's past quarterly and annual reports in the ASX record landed between 08:44 and 09:54 AEST, except the 2023 annual report at 17:57. Checked against the ASX archive (URL above), but moot because the date itself is unconfirmed.
positioning_check: ASIC aggregate short is 12.39% as of 2026-09-21 (44.9m shares), up from 11.72% on 2026-09-14 (+0.67pp, still building). The lag is 4 sessions, so the most recent reading predates the 22 to 25 September slide from A$3.03 to A$2.76. That is a crowded short by ASX standards and would be squeeze fuel on a clean set of audited accounts. Pointing the other way, the last set of financial statements (Half Year Accounts, 2026-03-12) was followed by -14.3%, -14.1% and -22.2% over three sessions and an ASX price query about grant-reimbursement accounting (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260316/pdf/06xgs30n99z9gg.pdf). So the audited accounts are a live two-sided risk on this name, but I found no document that signs it. Vanguard's 603 (5.08% on 2026-09-18) records roughly 1.1m shares bought at A$2.98 on 18 September. That looks like an index-rebalance print, which is passive and already priced.

outside_window.finding: The FY2026 Annual Report (audited June-2026 accounts, auditor opinion) is statutorily due by 2026-09-30. Last year it landed on the deadline day, and a MarketBeat-listed call at 29 Sep 19:00 ET maps to 30 Sep AEST. If it lands on 29 or 30 September it falls outside this window. Its direction is unsigned: the cash numbers are already public, and the only company-specific precedent is the -40% three-session slide after the half-year accounts in March 2026, against a 12.4% short that is still building.
